statement: Microsoft released software updates to plug nearly 200 security holes across Windows operating systems and supported software, a record number of fixes for the company's monthly Patch Tuesday cycle.
CVE-2026-49160, a denial of service vulnerability affecting Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS), was reported by OpenAI's Codex.

Satnam Narang from Tenable stated that surveys put AI usage among security professionals generally at 90%, and that this volume of patches may become the norm as more advanced AI models become available.
Microsoft patched 360 browser vulnerabilities in June 2026, described as an order of magnitude more than typical in any given month over the past few years.
At least 72 of Microsoft's public code repositories were infected with a variant of the Shai-Hulud worm, all connected to Microsoft official Azure Durable Task SDK.

Anthropic reported in May 2026 that it and approximately 50 partners used Claude Mythos Preview to find more than 10,000 high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities in systemically important software in a single month.
When pointed at Firefox, the Claude Mythos Preview model wrote 181 working exploits, compared to 2 from the previous frontier model.
Claude Mythos Preview surfaced an OpenBSD bug that had sat undetected for 27 years, and more than 99% of what it found was still unpatched at the time of writing.
Zero Day Clock reports that the average time-to-exploit (TTE) in 2026 is roughly 24 hours, down from approximately 53 days in 2024.

Verizon's 2026 DBIR ties 32% of initial-access techniques to exploitation of vulnerabilities and expects that number to climb, as AI coding assistants now put exploit-building within reach for attackers who've never had it before.
The Verizon 2026 DBIR tracked 13,000+ organizations and found that median fix time for known-exploited vulnerabilities was 43 days, up from 32 days the year before.
The Verizon 2026 DBIR found that the amount of known-exploited vulnerabilities that were fully patched was 26%, down from 38% the year before.
The median organization had to patch 16 known-exploited vulnerabilities in 2025, up from 11 the year before, representing a jump of nearly 50%.
An AWS threat-intelligence report from February 2026 documented an AI-augmented attack using a custom MCP server running offensive tools autonomously that affected 600+ devices across 55+ countries.
Nightmare Eclipse released 'YellowKey,' an exploit for a Windows BitLocker vulnerability that allows an attacker with physical access to view encrypted data.

A coalition of AI leaders, biotechnology executives, scientists, public health experts and national security officials sent a letter to U.S. lawmakers calling for legislation to require companies that produce synthetic DNA and RNA to screen every order and keep records of the people placing them.

Signatories to the synthetic DNA screening letter include the CEOs of Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Microsoft AI and OpenAI, as well as executives at academic institutions, Nobel laureates, DNA synthesis providers and former government officials.

The letter states that advances in AI could make it easier for bad actors to design and re-create dangerous pathogens, and that AI systems improving rapidly means knowledge barriers which have historically prevented bad actors from obtaining biological weapons will meaningfully erode.

The signatories are requesting federal legislation that requires providers of synthesized DNA and manufacturers of synthesis machines to keep detailed records, verify customer legitimacy before shipping an order, examine synthesis requests for sequences of concern, and record synthesis orders and sequence data to support potential biosecurity investigations.

On June 10, 2026, Anthropic announced the launch of Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, which the company said exceed any model made generally available and demonstrate exceptional capabilities in scientific research.

Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models demonstrated strong biological reasoning by completing a complex gene therapy research task involving adeno-associated viruses (AAVs), a capability Anthropic said could accelerate drug development while also posing biosecurity risks.

On June 10, 2026, Anthropic announced it was disabling access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers to ensure compliance with a U.S. government export control directive that required suspension of access for foreign nationals inside and outside the U.S., including foreign-national Anthropic employees.
The International Gene Synthesis Consortium was formed in 2009 to develop and implement voluntary safeguards against misuse of synthetic nucleic acids.
OpenAI analyzed approximately 1.3 million de-identified conversations across GPT-5 Thinking through GPT-5.4 deployments, spanning August 2025 to March 2026.
Deployment Simulation had a median multiplicative error of 1.5x when predicting undesired model behavior rates, where tail errors can reach roughly 10x.
Automated auditing in OpenAI's Deployment Simulation pipeline surfaced calculator hacking before release, which was the only novel misalignment identified in the analyzed ChatGPT traffic.
GPT-5.2 labeled real production traffic as evaluation-like 5.4% of the time and simulated traffic 5.1% of the time.
OpenAI used 120,000 internal employee agentic trajectories from GPT-5.4 to simulate the internal deployment of coding agents based on GPT-5.5.
WildChat-based Deployment Simulation had lower average multiplicative error than recent OpenAI production data at 2.44× versus 1.75×.
TraceMap is a Commission AI-powered tool that helps to speed up the detection of food fraud and foodborne incidents and outbreaks in any EU country.
TraceMap enables authorities to search, filter and extract relevant data with advanced AI from EU agri-food databases including TRACES, ACN and RASFF.
Before TraceMap, tracing products and operators across the supply chain meant relying largely on manual document checks and direct exchanges between authorities.
The European Commission published draft, non-binding guidelines on the classification of high-risk AI systems on 19 May 2026.
Draft guidelines on high-risk AI systems are open for public consultation until 23 June 2026.
Complex systems made up of several AI components, including agentic AI systems, must be assessed holistically and cannot rely on the Article 6(3) filter individually unless genuinely separable.
Emotion recognition systems that infer emotions or intentions from biometric signals such as voice, facial expressions, or posture are classified as high-risk under Annex III.
For fraud detection exception under point 5(b) of Annex III, an AI system's main intended use must be fraud detection; systems primarily used for creditworthiness evaluation are high-risk.
Research Ireland and the Irish Government are investing €17m across nine infrastructure projects in STEM fields including semiconductors, medical devices, quantum and AI computing.

The largest individual infrastructure award is €4.67m for an advanced semiconductor processing and characterisation facility for multifunctional thin-film materials at Tyndall National Institute, led by Dr Lynette Keeney.
An atomic layer etch diagnostic platform at Dublin City University, overseen by Prof Deborah O'Connell, will be funded to the tune of €2.89m for developing and studying materials at the atomic scale.
A medical device innovation network will receive €1.97m to establish a national research facility developed in partnership between the University of Galway and RCSI.
Of the nine lead researchers affiliated with the new Irish facilities, six are women and three are men.

The nine infrastructure awards are allocated across three facilities in advanced materials, two in semiconductors and chips, and one each in high-speed communications, medical devices, geoengineering, and AI and high-performance computing.
Code with Claude, Anthropic's two-day developer event, kicked off on May 19, 2026 in London, the same day as Google's I/O in Palo Alto.
At Code with Claude in London, almost half the developers in the audience raised their hands when asked if they had shipped a pull request in the last week that was completely written by Claude.
When asked a follow-up question whether they had shipped a pull request completely written by Claude without reading the code at all, most of the hands that were raised earlier stayed up.
Most software at Anthropic is now written by Claude, according to Jeremy Hadfield, an engineer at Anthropic, who stated that Claude has written most of the code in Claude Code.
Boris Cherny, who heads Claude Code, stated that the default is now 'I'm going to have Claude prompt itself' rather than 'I'm going to prompt Claude.'
Claude 4.6 and Claude 4.7 were released in February and April 2026 respectively, improving Claude Code's capabilities.
A new feature in Claude Managed Agents called 'dreaming' allows Claude agents to write notes to themselves and save useful information about specific tasks for other agents to use.
Companies including Spotify and Delivery Hero have reshaped their software development teams around Claude Code, along with startups Lovable, Base44, and Monday.com.

Katelyn Lesse, Claude engineering lead at Anthropic, stated that Claude is probably as good as a midlevel engineer at writing code but that expert engineers are still needed to design systems and troubleshoot harder problems.
Katelyn Lesse reported that some technical managers at Anthropic are exhausted by keeping up with all the code their teams now produce.
Angela Jiang, Claude product lead at Anthropic, stated that the absolute end state they are trying to get to is Claude being able to build itself.
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and will be fully applicable on 2 August 2026.
Prohibited AI practices and AI literacy obligations entered into application from 2 February 2025.
Governance rules and obligations for GPAI models became applicable on 2 August 2025.
Rules for high-risk AI systems embedded into regulated products have an extended transition period until 2 August 2028.
Rules for systems used in certain high-risk areas including biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum and border control will apply from 2 December 2027.
For AI systems integrated into products such as lifts or toys, rules will apply from 2 August 2028.
The EU AI Act prohibits AI systems that generate non-consensual sexually explicit and intimate content or child sexual abuse material.
Regulatory sandboxes obligation for Member States is postponed from 2 August 2026 to 2 August 2027.
On 7 May 2026, the Council and European Parliament reached a provisional political agreement on targeted amendments to the AI Act.
The final compromise text on AI Act amendments was published on 13 May 2026.

Two new implementation milestones for high-risk AI system obligations are 2 December 2027 for standalone high-risk AI systems within Annex III and 2 August 2028 for AI systems embedded as safety components in products governed by sectoral EU safety legislation.

High-risk AI systems already on the market before 2 December 2027 (for Annex III systems) or before 2 August 2028 (for Annex I systems) will benefit from the grace period, provided their design remains unchanged.
On 19 May 2026 the Commission published draft guidelines on the classification of high-risk artificial intelligence systems under the EU AI Act.
A four-month grace period for watermarking obligations on Article 50 allows generative AI systems already on market before 2 August 2026 to comply by 2 December 2026.
Providers have until 2 December 2026 to bring any AI systems generating non-consensual intimate content or CSAM into compliance.
Providers and deployers are now required to take appropriate measures to support the development of AI literacy among their staff, framed as an obligation of effort, not of result.
The AI Act now formally recognises small mid-cap enterprises (SMCs) and extends simplified requirements previously granted only to SMEs to small mid-cap companies.
The EU AI Office may impose periodic penalty payments of up to 5% of average daily income or annual worldwide turnover per day for continued non-compliance, with a five-year limitation period.
The Commission must adopt guidance including a post-market monitoring template by 2 September 2027.
By 2 August 2027, each Member State must establish at least one AI testing environment (sandbox), alone or together with others.
The EU AI Office gains exclusive supervisory and enforcement competence over AI systems built on general-purpose AI (GPAI) models where the model and system share the same provider.

Where high-risk AI systems fall within the scope of the Cyber Resilience Act and its conditions are fulfilled, such systems shall be deemed to comply with cybersecurity requirements of Article 15 of the AI Act.
The amendments to the AI Act remain subject to approval by both the European Parliament and the Council, with adoption envisaged before 2 August 2026.
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024.
Prohibited AI practices and AI literacy obligations entered into application from 2 February 2025.
The governance rules and the obligations for GPAI models became applicable on 2 August 2025.
Rules for systems used in certain high-risk areas will apply from 2 December 2027.
For systems integrated into products such as lifts or toys, the rules will apply from 2 August 2028.
A political agreement on the AI Act amendments was reached on 7 May 2026.
AI systems that generate non-consensual sexually explicit and intimate content or child sexual abuse material are prohibited.
The AI Office's powers will be reinforced and will have centralised oversight of AI systems built on general-purpose AI models.
Simplified technical documentation requirements for SMEs and small mid-cap companies are extended.
More innovators will gain access to regulatory sandboxes, including an EU-level sandbox.
Ireland will adopt a distributed model of competent authorities for the AI Act, as approved by Government Decisions of 4 March 2025 and 22 July 2025.

statement: PwC's 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer analysed more than one billion jobs advertisements across six continents
Jobs requiring specific AI skills are growing 69% faster than the total jobs market at 9% growth
The average wage premium for AI skills reached 62%, up from 57% in the previous year
AI-exposed entry-level roles are seven times more likely to require traditionally senior-level skills like leadership and creativity
'Seniorised' entry-level roles grew 35% since 2019, while other entry-level roles declined 10%
Companies most able to use AI achieved labour productivity gains of 163% ('super-star' effect), nearly five times higher than the most AI-exposed companies overall
Companies most AI-exposed saw headcount growth of 52% versus 36% for least AI-exposed companies in 2025 on 2018 baseline
Technology, media and telecommunications sector saw 11% share of AI job growth, while professional services saw 6% and health saw less than 1%
'Professionalised' roles are seeing twice the growth in available jobs and 42% faster salary growth than 'democratised' roles
Productivity growth was 34% for companies in most AI-exposed sectors relative to 2018, versus 24% for least AI-exposed companies
Anthropic's observed exposure measure combines theoretical LLM capability and real-world usage data, weighting automated and work-related uses more heavily
Computer programmers are most exposed to AI with 75% task coverage in Anthropic's analysis, followed by customer service representatives
Data entry keyers are 67% covered by AI capability in Anthropic's analysis
30% of workers have zero AI coverage, including cooks, motorcycle mechanics, lifeguards, bartenders, dishwashers and dressing room attendants
For every 10 percentage point increase in Anthropic's observed exposure measure, BLS employment growth projections drop by 0.6 percentage points
Workers most exposed to AI are 16 percentage points more likely to be female, 11 percentage points more likely to be white, and almost twice as likely to be Asian compared to unexposed workers
Workers most exposed to AI earn 47% more on average than unexposed workers
Graduate degree holders comprise 17.4% of the most AI-exposed group versus 4.5% of unexposed workers
Anthropic found no systematic increase in unemployment for highly exposed workers since late 2022
Job finding rates for workers aged 22-25 entering highly exposed occupations fell by about 14% post-ChatGPT compared to 2022
97% of tasks observed in Anthropic Economic Index reports fall into categories rated as theoretically feasible by Eloundou et al.
Claude usage accounts for 68% of observed tasks rated as fully feasible for LLM alone (β=1), while 3% account for tasks not feasible (β=0)
Claude currently covers 33% of all tasks in the Computer & Math occupational category
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and will be fully applicable on 2 August 2026.
Prohibited AI practices and AI literacy obligations entered into application on 2 February 2025.
The governance rules and obligations for GPAI models became applicable on 2 August 2025.
Rules for high-risk AI systems embedded into regulated products have an extended transition period until 2 August 2028.

Rules for high-risk AI systems used in certain high-risk areas including biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum and border control will apply from 2 December 2027.
Rules for high-risk AI systems integrated into products such as lifts or toys will apply from 2 August 2028.
The 'AI omnibus' proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025 and a political agreement was reached on 7 May 2026.

The AI Act prohibits eight practices: harmful AI-based manipulation and deception, harmful AI-based exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, individual criminal offence risk assessment or prediction, untargeted scraping of the internet or CCTV material to create or expand facial recognition databases, emotion recognition in workplaces and education institutions, biometric categorisation to deduce certain protected characteristics, and real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement purposes in publicly accessible spaces.

A prohibition of AI systems that generate non-consensual sexually explicit and intimate content or child sexual abuse material, such as AI 'nudification' apps, has been agreed as part of amendments to the AI Act.

The AI Office's powers have been reinforced and oversight of AI systems built on general-purpose AI models has been centralised to reduce governance fragmentation, as part of amendments agreed in May 2026.

Simplified requirements granted to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have been extended to small mid-cap companies (SMCs), including simplified technical documentation requirements, as part of amendments agreed in May 2026.
More innovators will gain access to regulatory sandboxes, including an EU-level sandbox, to test AI solutions in real-world conditions, as part of amendments agreed in May 2026.

The interplay between the AI Act and EU product safety laws, in particular the Machinery Regulation, has been clarified to avoid duplication between sectoral and AI rules, as part of amendments agreed in May 2026.
The General Scheme of the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026 was published on 4 February 2026 and last updated on 9 February 2026.

statement: Over 2 million hosts with 1 million exposed AI services were identified through certificate transparency logs scanning.
A significant number of exposed AI hosts had been deployed straight out of the box with no authentication in place.
ClawdBot, a self-hosted AI assistant, is averaging 2.6 CVEs per day.
Over 90 exposed instances of agent management platforms like n8n and Flowise were identified across government, marketing, and finance sectors.
Of 5,200+ Ollama servers queried, 31% responded to a basic prompt without requiring authentication.
2,130 AI-related CVEs were disclosed in 2025, representing a 34.6% year-over-year increase.
TrendAI Research analysis identified 6,086 unique vulnerabilities disclosed from 2018 to 2025 that directly affect AI systems.
Nearly half of scored AI vulnerabilities are categorized as high- or critical-severity, particularly in emerging areas like agentic AI and MCP servers.
1,467 exposed MCP servers were discovered, representing a nearly threefold increase from initial findings.
1,227 of 1,467 exposed MCP servers are running the deprecated Server-Sent Events (SSE) transport protocol.
An execute_sql tool was available on 70 publicly accessible MCP hosts, allowing unauthorized SQL query execution.
Between 2,800 and 3,600 AI CVEs are projected for 2026, representing a 31-69% increase from 2025.
Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5 preview and Claude Mythos 5 general availability in early June 2026
OpenAI released GPT-5.6 in June 2026 as part of a six-week release cadence
Google rolled out Gemini 3.2 as a mid-cycle multimodal refresh in June 2026
Twelve distinct frontier or near-frontier LLM releases shipped within the first two weeks of June 2026
Claude Mythos 5 moved from April 2026 partner preview into general availability in June 2026
Claude Fable 5 remains in closed partner preview as of June 10, 2026 with no announced general availability date
DeepSeek V4.1 represents a 15% per-token reduction compared to V4 Flash
Anthropic disabled access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models after the U.S. government imposed export controls, citing national security concerns
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis called for a U.S.-led AI coalition at a G7 summit meeting on June 17, 2026
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman called for an international forum for discussion that would establish international standards for testing and serve as a venue for cooperation among nations

SK Telecom, South Korea's largest carrier and a $100 million Anthropic investor since 2023, was identified by the White House as a company suspected of having ties to China with access to Claude Mythos, triggering the initial request to revoke its access.

Amazon researchers separately identified potential vulnerabilities in Fable 5 and reported them to the White House, which escalated the ban from revoking only SK Telecom's access to blocking all foreign nationals from both Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models globally.

Chris Ciauri, Anthropic's Managing Director of International, stated at the Seoul press conference on June 17-18: 'We are very confident that in the coming days, the models will become available again.'

David Sacks, Co-Chair of the President's Council of Advisers on Science and Technology (PCAST), disclosed that the Trump administration offered Anthropic a choice before issuing the export control directive: either fix the identified jailbreak in Fable 5 or voluntarily de-deploy the model. Dario Amodei refused both options.

OpenAI is acquiring Astral, the company behind uv (a fast Python package installer and resolver) and ruff (a Python linter and code formatter), with the stated goal of integrating its tools into Codex, OpenAI's AI-assisted software development platform.

Anthropic signed a Memorandum of Understanding with South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT, committing both parties to collaborate on AI safety and cybersecurity, including evaluating model safety in the Korean language with the Korea AI Safety Institute.
entities: South Korea Ministry of Science and ICT

statement: NAVER deployed Claude Code across its entire engineering organization with thousands of engineers now using Claude Code to diversify their coding tools and maximize coding productivity.
Samsung SDS is deploying Claude, including Claude Cowork and Claude Code, across Samsung Electronics for knowledge work, agentic workflows, and software development at scale.
LG CNS is deploying Claude to thousands of employees and plans to extend access across LG Group as a whole.
Hanwha Solutions is deploying Claude globally through AWS Bedrock with in-region data residency and security requirements.
Nexon, the global online game developer, has deployed Claude Code for its live-service game engineering, writing, reviewing, and shipping code for games played by millions globally.
Claude Code weekly active users in Korea grew 6x in four months.
Large-business accounts above $100,000 in annualized revenue in Asia-Pacific grew 8x for Anthropic.
Dario Amodei had three separate calls with cabinet officials including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick after the export control directive on June 12.
Anthropic issued refunds for subscribers who signed up between June 9-14 when Fable 5 was live, with a June 20, 2026 deadline for refund processing.
The Fable 5 free-trial window for paid subscribers (Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise) officially closes on June 22, 2026, after which subscription users need paid usage credits.

Anthropic launched Claude Corps, a national fellowship program for early-career Americans, providing structured access to Claude, mentorship, and community programs for social, civic, and community benefit use cases.
Anthropic doubled the usage limits for Claude Cowork—its desktop application for non-developer automation—at no additional charge to subscribers.
DXC Technology and Anthropic announced a partnership on June 11, 2026, to integrate Claude into enterprise IT systems for banks, airlines, hospitals, and other regulated industries.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Anthropic announced their global partnership on June 12, 2026, with TCS integrating Claude into its enterprise consulting and IT services across banking, financial services, retail, healthcare, and government sectors.
Google released its first smart speaker in approximately six years, featuring Gemini AI as the built-in assistant with natural conversation capabilities and advanced voice interaction features.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman postponed a planned visit to South Korea following the birth of his second daughter, including planned meetings with Samsung, Naver, and Kakao.

Trump administration officials told WIRED that Anthropic must proactively test all frontier AI models to identify potential jailbreaks and report them to the government before any relaunch of Fable 5, and must eliminate all jailbreaks from Claude Fable 5 before relaunching.
Prediction markets moved sharply on Ciauri's 'coming days' signal: Kalshi now prices a 57% chance Fable 5 returns before July 1, 67% before July 10, and 75% before July 17.
Eight well-written examples in a prompt were enough for a 540-billion parameter model to beat fine-tuned GPT-3 on the GSM8K math benchmark.
A 2024 study by OpenAI showed that structured prompts produce output preferred by human annotators in 73% of cases compared to unstructured prompts on free-form writing tasks.
In 'Game of 24', GPT-4 with standard Chain-of-Thought solved only 4% of problems, while with Tree of Thoughts the percentage jumped to 74%.
ReAct beats imitation learning and reinforcement learning methods by 34% in absolute success rate on ALFWorld with one or two in-context examples.
Self-Refine shows an average 20% performance improvement across 7 different tasks with GPT-3.5, ChatGPT and GPT-4 without training or supervised data.
A test of two follow-up email prompts on 50 real clients in 2025 found the structured prompt (CREATE + Chain-of-Thought) got a reply 64% of the time versus 19% for the basic prompt.
Anthropic put context engineering in writing on their engineering blog in 'Effective context engineering for AI agents'.
Stanford released DSPy in late 2023 and by 2026 it has reached version 2.x with the MIPROv2 optimizer.
DSPy shows 10-40% quality improvements compared to manual prompting on RAG pipelines and classifiers.

Anthropic launched Project Glasswing on April 7, 2026, giving Claude Mythos Preview to roughly 50 partner organizations including AWS, Apple, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, CrowdStrike, and JPMorgan Chase for defensive cybersecurity work only.
The Project Glasswing first-month report from May 22, 2026 states Claude Mythos found 23,019 vulnerabilities across 1,000+ open-source projects with 90.6% confirmed real on independent sampling.
Gemini 3.5 Flash went GA on May 19 at Google I/O 2026 with API pricing at $1.50 per million input tokens and $9.00 per million output tokens.
Gemini 3.5 Flash beats Gemini 3.1 Pro at roughly 4x the speed on coding and agentic benchmarks.
Gemini 3.5 Pro was announced at Google I/O with Sundar Pichai stating 'give us until next month to get it to you', confirmed for June but with no specific date provided.
A Sonnet 4.8 source map accidentally shipped with @anthropic-ai/claude-code npm v2.1.88 on March 31, 2026, containing source filter lists with the strings sonnet-4-8, opus-4-7, and mythos.
Polymarket closed at 3% on a Sonnet 4.8 ship date of May 24, 2026.
Grok 5 is still training on Colossus 2 expanded from 1 GW to 1.5 GW in April with reported specs of ~6 trillion parameters MoE, 1.5M context, and native multimodal.
Polymarket contract for Grok 5 public release by June 30, 2026 collapsed from 68 cents in February to 12% by early April and currently sits in the 12–33% range.
The Trump administration ordered Anthropic to suspend all access to the latest version of its Mythos Fable 5 software, citing security concerns.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told G7 leaders he understood concerns that AI tools could be used by bad actors but said democratic nations should avoid becoming divided over how AI tools are rolled out.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman called for an international forum for discussion that would establish international standards for testing, give impartial expert analysis of risks and serve as a venue for cooperation among nations.

French President Emmanuel Macron said the Anthropic situation had raised fears for many in Europe that the Trump administration could block non-U.S. companies from accessing AI models, even if the countries were friendly to the U.S.

Following the EU AI Act Omnibus (provisional political agreement, 7 May 2026), the main high-risk deadline has been deferred with Annex III systems (recruitment, credit scoring, law enforcement) required to comply by 2 December 2027.
Annex I systems embedded in regulated products must comply with EU AI Act high-risk obligations by 2 August 2028.

GPAI model obligations under Articles 51–55 of the EU AI Act have applied since 2 August 2025; new models placed on the market after 2 August 2025 must comply immediately, while models already on the market before that date have until 2 August 2027.

Transparency obligations under Article 50 of the EU AI Act take effect 2 August 2026; AI systems that interact directly with people must disclose this, and synthetic audio, image, video, and text content must be labelled in a machine-readable format.

Article 5 prohibitions of the EU AI Act have been enforceable since 2 February 2025 with violations carrying fines up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover, covering social scoring, manipulative AI, and biometric categorisation.
The EU AI Act is extraterritorial; UK organisations placing AI systems on the EU market or whose AI outputs affect EU users are in scope regardless of where they are headquartered.
The transparency rules of the AI Act will come into effect in August 2026.
Rules for systems used in certain high-risk areas including biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum and border control will apply from 2 December 2027.
A prohibition of AI systems that generate non-consensual sexually explicit and intimate content or child sexual abuse material has been agreed as an amendment to the AI Act.
The AI Office's powers have been reinforced and oversight of AI systems built on general-purpose AI models has been centralized to reduce governance fragmentation.
Simplified requirements for small and medium-sized enterprises have been extended to small mid-cap companies, including simplified technical documentation requirements.
The European Commission has published draft non-binding guidelines on high-risk AI system classification under the Digital Omnibus amendments, with a consultation window closing June 23.
The primary Annex III high-risk AI compliance deadline has been deferred by 16 months to December 2, 2027.
The European Commission has published finalized Article 50 transparency guidelines and two standardized AI content labeling icons.
Deployers of AI content systems have fewer than 53 days to implement disclosure obligations before the August 2, 2026 enforcement deadline.
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, and will be fully applicable 2 years later on 2 August 2026.
The Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026, once enacted, will give effect in Ireland to the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689).

statement: A comprehensive case study on Irish Mental Health Services (MHS) found that psychiatrists and mental health professionals rated their Mental Health Department's processes for IT use and digital practices at an average score of 4.37 out of 10 (SD 1.25).
In a survey of Irish mental health professionals, 75% (n=12) reported that staff members are allowed to keep their phones while accessing psychiatric case notes.
In a survey of Irish mental health professionals, 80% (n=13) highlighted that multiple staff members can access sensitive psychiatric notes and patients' contact information.

A case study of Irish Mental Health Services found that 90% of respondents (n=15) reported that patients' private thoughts and mental challenges described to psychologists or psychiatrists are stored on paper-based charts or forms.

A study of Irish Mental Health Services survey participants estimated that a proposed technological solution combining speech-to-text transcription, AI analysis, and permissioned blockchain storage would optimize their workload by an average of 35%.

Ireland is ranked among the most disadvantageous European countries in terms of mental health challenges, with a Mental Health Quotient score of 56 placing it as the second worst in Europe according to the Mental State of the World Report 2022.
entities: Mental State of the World Report

statement: According to Mental State of the World Report 2022, Ireland had 30.4% of respondents classified as distressed or struggling, the second highest in the European countries measured after the United Kingdom at 35.7%.
entities: Mental State of the World Report 2022

statement: Mental health issues in Ireland cost the country €8.2 billion annually, according to figures cited in the study.

The Irish Mental Health Services study found that handwritten psychiatric case notes have alarmingly low readability, with one psychiatrist claiming that 70% of the contents of psychiatric case notes are not readable.

The study proposes that Irish Mental Health Services should implement speech-to-text transcription for data collection, interactive AI for data analysis, and permissioned blockchain for data storage and retrieval.
In 2023, European Union countries reported 309 major cybersecurity incidents in the healthcare sector, the highest among all critical sectors.
Productivity growth is 40% higher at companies most exposed to AI versus least.
Skills needed for the most AI-exposed jobs are changing more than twice as fast as for the least AI-exposed jobs.
Seniorised entry level roles are showing 35% growth since 2019, while overall early-career job postings have flatlined in highly AI exposed sectors.
The most AI exposed junior roles are 7 times more likely than the least AI exposed junior roles to demand traditionally senior skills like leadership.
Professionalised jobs are growing twice as fast as democratised jobs, with 42% faster wage growth since 2021.
Of the S&P Global 1200 index, 994 participants (83%) had a lower head count in January 2026 compared to January 2025, with just 153 (13%) experiencing an increase.
The latest S&P Global Purchasing Managers' Index survey shows a global net impact of -5 percentage points over the past 12 months and a further -2 points net impact forecast for the coming year.
Among enterprise AI objectives, process efficiency (64%) and employee productivity (59%) are much more commonly prioritized than head count reduction (24%).
Only 46% of AI initiatives launched in the past year are deemed on track to achieve positive ROI within 12 months, and only 37% are assessed as live and delivering value.
Only 22% of AI projects target a fully autonomous end state, where AI operates without human intervention.
Large companies forecast a net negative employment impact from AI of -13 points, while small firms continue to forecast a net positive employment effect of +3 points and medium-sized firms +2 points.
Among large enterprises with 10,000+ employees, 44% cite a clear, documented AI strategy aligned with core business goals.
Confidence in third-party AI models has fallen markedly: in 2026, just 16% completely trust them while 30% mostly trust them, down from 24% and 42% respectively in 2023.
Among AI use cases, the average current adoption rate is 50%, and the average planned adoption rate in the next year is 37%.
Cybersecurity skills gaps had a moderate or severe impact on AI initiatives for 64% of respondents, the highest shortage impact among technical functions.
The European Parliament approved, by a large majority, legislative amendments to the EU AI Act following a plenary vote on 16 June 2026.
A political agreement on the Digital Omnibus on AI was reached on 7 May 2026 between negotiators from the Council of the European Union, the European Parliament, and the European Commission.
The obligations concerning the detection and labelling of AI-generated content (Article 50 of the EU AI Act) will become applicable on 2 December 2026.
AI systems capable of generating child sexual abuse material are prohibited from being placed on the EU market under amendments to the EU AI Act.

AI systems capable of creating images, videos, or audio recordings depicting an individual as nude, partially nude, or engaged in sexually explicit conduct without consent are prohibited from being placed on the EU market under amendments to the EU AI Act.

Eight AI practices are banned under the EU AI Act, including harmful AI-based manipulation and deception, harmful AI-based exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, individual criminal offence risk assessment, untargeted scraping for facial recognition databases, emotion recognition in workplaces and education, biometric categorisation for protected characteristics, and real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement in public spaces.
Prohibitions on certain AI systems and AI literacy requirements (Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 of the AI Act) entered into application from 2 February 2025.

AI functionalities that merely provide user assistance or optimise product performance without creating health or safety risks will no longer be automatically classified as high-risk under amendments to the EU AI Act.

Personal data may be processed for identifying and mitigating bias in both high-risk and non-high-risk AI systems, subject to appropriate technical and organisational safeguards, under amendments to the EU AI Act.
Federal agencies must begin hardening their information systems with AI-enabled cyber defenses within 30 days of June 2, 2026.

The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the National Cyber Director, the Secretary of War, and the Secretary of Homeland Security, shall form an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse within 30 days to coordinate scanning for software vulnerabilities, discover and validate vulnerabilities, and coordinate remediation and distribution of vulnerability patches.

The updated 2026 CVE forecast projects approximately 66,000 CVEs for the full year, up from the February median of 59,427, marking the first time in history that annual vulnerability disclosures are on pace to approach 70,000.
source_name: FIRST (Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams)

statement: Actual CVE disclosures through April 2026 are running 46.3% above the projections published in February 2026, with 6,420 excess CVEs recorded.
source_name: FIRST (Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams)

statement: Three structural drivers of the 2026 CVE surge include AI-assisted vulnerability discovery, a 449% year-over-year surge in GitHub Security Advisory (GHSA) volume, and a 3,119% increase in VulnCheck CNA-of-Last-Resort activity.
source_name: FIRST (Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams)

statement: When filtered for real-world risk (CISA KEV entries or EPSS scores above 10%), actionable exploitability remains flat and the patching burden has not materially increased despite the surge in raw CVE volume.
source_name: FIRST (Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams)

statement: There was a 164% spike in Q1 CVE disclosures from the Mozilla CNA, directly attributable to AI-assisted tooling running against the Firefox engine.
source_name: FIRST (Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams)

statement: The number of distinct software products with tracked vulnerabilities has grown by two orders of magnitude, driving workload independent of AI or CNA changes.

statement: Twelve distinct frontier or near-frontier LLM releases shipped within the first two weeks of June 2026 across Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Alibaba, DeepSeek, Tencent, Baidu, ByteDance, Mistral, and Zhipu.
Claude Fable 5 remained in closed partner preview as of June 10, 2026 with no announced general availability date.
Claude Mythos 5 moved from April 2026 Project Glasswing partner preview to general availability in June 2026.
OpenAI released GPT-5.6 on a six-week release cadence in June 2026.
Google rolled out Gemini 3.2 as a mid-cycle multimodal refresh in June 2026.
DeepSeek V4.1 achieved a 15% per-token reduction on DeepSeek V4 Flash.
Qwen 3.7 undercuts DeepSeek V4 Flash on several configurations.
The cybersecurity frontier moved from preview to general availability with Claude Mythos 5, putting vulnerability-aware reasoning into enterprise procurement workflows.
The Chinese frontier set converged into a credible four-horse race consisting of Qwen, DeepSeek, Hunyuan, and GLM in June 2026.

DeepSeek V4 in April 2026 established a price-performance benchmark that forced Alibaba (Qwen 3.7), Tencent (Hunyuan Large 3), Baidu (ERNIE 5.1), ByteDance (Doubao Pro), and Zhipu (GLM-6) to respond rapidly.

statement: In May 2026, OpenAI reported that a reasoning model produced core ideas to disprove the Erdős unit-distance conjecture, an open problem in discrete geometry since 1946.
The AI model found point configurations where the count of unit-distance pairs can grow at least as fast as n^1.014, showing the Erdős unit-distance conjecture can be disproven.
Fields Medalist Tim Gowers called the AI disproof of the Erdős conjecture 'the first example of a result produced autonomously by an AI that I find exciting in itself.'

Google DeepMind released AI Co-Mathematician, an interactive workbench of AI agents supporting ideation, literature search, computational exploration, and theorem proving while tracking failed hypotheses across sessions.
AI Co-Mathematician scored 48% on FrontierMath Tier 4, the hardest tier of the benchmark, a new high among systems tested at the time.
The Automated Conjecture Resolution framework, revised in June 2026, pairs a reasoning agent that searches for proofs with a second agent that formalizes them in Lean 4 with machine-checking.

The Automated Conjecture Resolution team reports resolving an open problem in commutative algebra with essentially no human involvement and finding new counterexamples in algebraic groups and p-adic Hodge theory.
Tool-DC, a training-free divide-and-conquer loop for iterative tool selection, delivers up to +25.10% average gains on tool-calling benchmarks without fine-tuning.
Tool-DC brought a Qwen2.5-7B model to 83.16% on BFCL, surpassing OpenAI o3 and Claude Haiku 4.5 on that test.
TurboQuant, a training-free method by Google Research/DeepMind, compresses the LLM key-value cache to approximately 3.5 bits per channel with no measurable quality loss.
TurboQuant achieves roughly a 6x key-value cache memory reduction at 3.5 bits per channel with absolute quality neutrality versus full precision.
ARCQuant, a 4-bit weight-and-activation quantization scheme, achieved up to 3x speedup over FP16 on an RTX 5090 / RTX PRO 6000.

Researchers at Tufts paired neural networks with symbolic reasoning for robot vision-language-action tasks, achieving training energy at approximately 1% of a standard model's (34 minutes vs. 36+ hours).
The Tufts neuro-symbolic approach achieved 95% task success versus 34% for the conventional neural-only approach.

ScaleSWE, a pipeline mining millions of real GitHub pull requests, fine-tuned a Qwen-30B model to 64% resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified, built from 6 million pull requests across 5,200 repositories distilled to approximately 71,500 trajectories.
AgentHallu, a benchmark across 7 agent frameworks and 5 domains with 693 trajectories, tested whether models can pinpoint which step in a multi-step run caused a hallucination.
Across 13 leading models tested on AgentHallu, the best reached only 41.1% step-localization accuracy, with tool-use hallucinations the hardest to catch at 11.6%.
MIT researchers found that a small AI model can outperform the biggest AI models at 1 percent of the cost using the classic game 'Battleship' as a test bed.
MIT researchers created a new ChartNet training dataset to improve the accuracy of vision-language models used to analyze business trends or interpret scientific figures.
The European Commission appointed a Scientific Panel and an Advisory Forum to support enforcement of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Act.
The Scientific Panel brings together 60 world-leading independent experts with experience in frontier AI, engineering, technical auditing, industry and societal impact.
The Scientific Panel will focus on general-purpose AI (GPAI) models and systems, systemic risks, model classification, evaluation methodologies and cross-border market surveillance.
The Advisory Forum members come from academia, civil society and industry, including small and medium-sized enterprises and startups.
Key European Union agencies with permanent roles in the Advisory Forum include the EU Agency for Fundamental Rights, the EU Agency for Cybersecurity ENISA, and standardisation bodies.
A joint venture majority-owned by SoftBank Group and formed with Sesterce was selected to develop and operate a 1 GW AI data center campus in Bosquel, France.
The Bosquel data center campus forms a key part of SoftBank Group's broader 5 GW commitment announced as part of the 2026 Choose France summit.
Bosquel is located in the Hauts-de-France region and is positioned near Paris, Brussels, Amsterdam, London and Frankfurt.
The Bosquel campus will create 400 long-term skilled roles in data center operations, energy systems, security, maintenance, and advanced infrastructure management once operational.

The joint venture plans to establish a €10 million endowment fund jointly managed with the Hauts-de-France region to promote the use of AI in local businesses, schools, universities and community organizations.

The Bosquel campus plan was designed by architecture firm Patriarche and includes a community center serving as a meeting space for residents, local businesses, students, entrepreneurs and public stakeholders.

Shifting prompts from asking models to 'be an expert' to supplying expert context—prior failures ruled out, explicit constraints, and the true task goal—can materially improve AI output quality and reliability.
This method operationalizes structured prompt engineering by front-loading failure modes and boundary conditions, enabling large language models to reduce trial-and-error cycles and hallucinations.

Businesses can translate this into a repeatable template: list known dead-ends, define constraints like budgets or compliance rules, and state success metrics, which shortens iteration time for product specs, code generation, and analytics planning.

According to OpenAI's prompt engineering guide, updated in 2023, structured prompts that incorporate contextual details can improve output accuracy by up to 30 percent in tasks like content generation and problem-solving.
Research from Anthropic in 2023 showed that prompts mimicking expert thought processes yield higher quality responses in complex scenarios.
According to a McKinsey report from 2023, organizations adopting advanced prompting strategies could see productivity gains worth $2.6 trillion to $4.4 trillion annually by 2030.
As of early 2024, Google's Bard and Microsoft's Azure AI have incorporated prompt optimization features.
Startups such as PromptBase emerged in 2022 to offer pre-built expert prompts, generating over $10 million in revenue by 2024.
IBM's Watson platform introduced prompt engineering courses in 2023 to help enterprises overcome skill gaps.
The EU AI Act of 2024 mandates transparency in AI interactions, encouraging ethical prompting to avoid biased outputs.
Chain-of-thought reasoning, first documented in a 2022 paper by Google researchers, boosts reasoning tasks by 40 percent.
A 2023 study in the New England Journal of Medicine found AI models with expert-context prompts improved diagnostic accuracy by 25 percent over standard inputs.
By 2027, automated prompt optimization tools could become standard, according to Gartner forecasts from 2023.
Amazon's use of contextual prompts in recommendation engines increased sales by 35 percent as reported in their 2023 earnings.
Duolingo has integrated contextual prompting techniques since 2022 to personalize learning paths.
Deloitte's 2024 tech report indicates a 20 percent rise in AI-driven revenue streams by 2026.
DeepMind developed the AI Control Roadmap, a framework for building and managing advanced AI deployed within Google
AI agents could create $2.9 trillion in economic value in the U.S. alone by 2030
DeepMind's team analyzed one million coding agent tasks to refine safety protocols and build a live monitor for the Gemini Spark agent
DeepMind published a technical framework for policymakers titled 'Three Layers of Agent Security'

Without formal approval of the Omnibus, the EU AI Act's original high-risk compliance deadline of August 2, 2026 remains in place, while the Omnibus would push that deadline back to December 2027 at the earliest

statement: The AI Act prohibits eight practices: harmful AI-based manipulation and deception; harmful AI-based exploitation of vulnerabilities; social scoring; individual criminal offence risk assessment or prediction; untargeted scraping for facial recognition databases; emotion recognition in workplaces and education institutions; biometric categorisation to deduce protected characteristics; and real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement in publicly accessible spaces.
The prohibitions on eight AI practices under the AI Act became effective in February 2025.
The AI Act governance rules and obligations for general-purpose AI models became applicable on 2 August 2025.
A political agreement on simplified AI Act implementation was reached on 7 May 2026.

The EU Digital Omnibus agreement amended the AI Act to prohibit AI systems that generate non-consensual sexually explicit and intimate content or child sexual abuse material, such as AI 'nudification' apps.
Simplified technical documentation requirements for SMEs are extended to small and medium-sized companies under the Digital Omnibus agreement.
More innovators will gain access to regulatory sandboxes, including an EU-level sandbox, under the Digital Omnibus agreement to test AI solutions in real-world conditions.
The Digital Omnibus agreement clarified the interplay between the AI Act and EU product safety laws, in particular the Machinery Regulation, to avoid duplication between sectoral and AI rules.

Minister Peter Burke stated that Ireland is hosting an Oireachtas presidency and that meeting AI Act obligations will strengthen Ireland's position as an EU centre of excellence and digital regulatory hub.

statement: PwC's 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer analysed more than one billion job ads across six continents.
AI-exposed entry-level roles are seven times more likely to require traditionally senior-level skills such as leadership.
Entry-level roles most exposed to AI grew 35% since 2019, while other entry-level roles shrank 10%.
Jobs requiring specific AI skills grew roughly eight times (69%) as fast as the overall jobs market, at 9%.
The average wage premium for workers with AI skills hit 62%, up from 57% last year.
The number of AI jobs is almost twice as high as 2024, with growth in AI jobs outpacing all jobs since 2015.
Top 20% of most AI-exposed companies achieved average labour productivity growth of 163% relative to 2018.
Professionalised roles are seeing twice the growth in available jobs and 42% faster salary growth than democratised roles.
Technology, media and telecommunications sector saw 11% of all AI job growth, professional services saw 6%, health saw less than 1%.
Companies most able to use AI are seeing faster headcount growth (52%) than the least AI-exposed companies (36%).
